content:
Connor O'Brien: heads up - reminder on runtime rollback guardrails since we're doing more frequent runtime drops

Connor O'Brien: if you think we need to roll back serving-runtime in prod: 1) pause progressive delivery first 2) pin tag 3) lock auto-advance

Hiro Tanaka: +1. also pls don't use the old "rollback by re-running canary" trick. It can re-advance the controller. Use `rw-release pause` + `rw-release set-tag`.

Grace O'Connor: from incident side: if it's customer impact, declare SEV2/SEV1 early. rollback can be the mitigation, but we need the decision recorded (who approved + target tag).

Evelyn Hart: approvals reminder: IC ok is enough during SEV, but if this touches Dedicated premium tenants loop CS oncall ASAP.

ReleaseBot: :information_source: Release commands quick ref: `rw-release pause`, `rw-release set-tag`, `rw-release deploy`, `rw-release lock`. Docs: confluence://eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/runtime-release-pipeline-rollback-procedure

Connor O'Brien: also, for Hosted, do regions in order: smaller region first if possible, then the rest. avoid partial rollback where routing still sends to degraded pools.
